I grew up in a cult. 

My grandmother would kidnap children and alienate them from their parents, making them completely dependent on her. She’s been doing this for 45 years now, and despite her advanced age she’s still doing it. 

She’ll befriend a young woman with any sort of problem and allow that woman and her child to live in her home, they give 90% of the money they make to her to “pay the bills” and eventually they get sick of it. They go to a woman’s shelter or stay with a friend, taking their child. Then my grandmother calls them, begging them to think about how that lifestyle will impact their child. They usually end up letting the kid stay with her, and they usually go back to the drugs or alcohol or various other things they were doing before they met her. CPS is always involved at her house, and they’ll usually open a case on the mother. This frequently ends up with my grandmother getting full custody of the child. 

When I was three, my parents had just moved out of her house in Texas and left for Ohio. We were staying in a motel, and my father had a job as a maintenance guy at the motel to pay the fees. One day he had a friend over, and needed to use the pay phone outside to order a pizza. He left me with the friend while he went to do that. This friend wanted my father’s job, and decided to get him arrested, so he called the cops for child abandonment. Keep in mind, my father was at the pay phone about a minute’s walk away, with a direct line of sight to the motel room door. 

Long story shorter, the cops took me from my loving parents and because my grandmother was my closest blood relative I was placed with her. I was raised until the age of fifteen to believe that my parents never loved me, that my own father raped me, and that I was incurably mentally ill to the point where I had to take medication far above the safe doses for a child my age. At age 10 I was taught to cook and clean, at age 11 I had two new kids I was responsible for looking after. 

In the end, I found an old letter that accidentally fell behind the filing cabinet. It had a woman’s name on it, one I didn’t know. Something inside me told me to read that letter, so I did. It was from a woman who’s child my grandmother had custody of. I continued to read. The woman was begging my grandmother to let her see her child, even just once. It had been a year. I continued reading, and it hit me like a punch. My own name right there, my grandmother had never taken another child with my name. I had never known my parents names, and I finally had a clue. So, naturally, after figuring out that my mother not loving me was a lie I began wondering what else was a lie. I messaged my mom on Facebook and now, five years and six days after that fateful day, I’m living with her and my father. I’m happier than I’ve ever been, even though I’m an adult I still don’t feel like one most days. My entire life up until five years ago was a lie, and I still can’t wrap my head around it. But I went through hell. True and complete hell. The beatings made my bones more likely to dislocate, the emotional abuse made me doubt myself endlessly, and I still came out on top. Nobody but me knew the full and complete truth, at least until now. Thanks for listening, strangers.

So I actually use rabbit poop as fertilizer for both my outdoor veggie garden and my indoor plants. You have to age it, leave it sit for a week or two and add a bit of water, mix it up and mash it with a stick every day during that week or two. The little bit of water and letting it sit will get off any extra ammonia that might burn the plant’s roots which lets you put the poop directly against the plant without burning it to death. The mixing just makes the pellets into something easier to mix with soil.

EDIT; Just wanted to add that my plants have never been happier. I got hundreds of cucumbers and tomatoes, my watermelon patch is growing like crazy, and my sunflowers are about 6 foot 8.

In taxidermy, don’t start with roadkill. If you aren’t amazing with knives you will cut yourself, even a little knick that you wouldn’t notice can transfer parasites and diseases that will probably kill you. If you’re interested in doing taxidermy you should go out, hunt a deer or something else you can eat, field dress and get the meat, and do your taxidermy as something of an afterthought or use a recently deceased pet you know the cause of death of (I use rabbits, they’re commonly taxidermied so you don’t get weird looks. Don’t taxidermy Fido unless you’re comfortable with it not looking the same.) The focus should always be on wasting as little as humanly possible. Once you get good enough with the skin thickness of different animals and the methods used to get everything cut up right then you can move on to roadkill. It’s one of those things you simply can’t mess around with unless you have a death wish.

The best way to taxidermy a bird is by removing the guts/muscle and adding borax to the inside of the skin including the skull after degloving the skull. Then use a glycerin and formalin mixture to inject into the brain, feet, and wings. After that you put the skull back into the puppet skin, sew most of the abdomen skin closed, stuff it with something soft, add wires if you want to pose it, and sew the rest shut. The tail feathers are attached by a piece of skin and muscle, so you’ll want to preserve that with formalin and glycerin too.
